text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for agreeing to see this two-year-old boy for an expert immunological assessment. His difficulties began shortly after birth, with his initial clinical symptoms emerging on his third day of life. He recently required hospitalization for an acute pulmonary parenchymal infection, presenting with dense infiltrates on chest imaging and respiratory distress that eventually stabilized with supportive care and broad-spectrum coverage.

Our investigations have highlighted a profound, overarching combined failure of both his cellular and antibody-mediated immune defenses. His peripheral blood counts show a marked depression of his total lymphocyte numbers. Humoral evaluation demonstrated distinctly subnormal serum IgA levels alongside severely depleted systemic IgM concentrations. Furthermore, specialized functional assays revealed a blunted T-lymphocyte blastogenic response following mitogenic stimulation.

Aside from the recent lung infection, his physical examination has been largely reassuring. His cardiovascular exam is normal with a regular rhythm and no murmurs, and his abdomen is soft, non-tender, and free of any palpable organomegaly. Neurological tone is age-appropriate, and he has reached his gross motor milestones on schedule. He lives at home with both parents and a healthy older sibling. There is no known parental consanguinity or family history of early childhood loss. He is currently maintained on prophylactic trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

I would appreciate your urgent evaluation and recommendations regarding further specialized management for his extensive dual-compartment immune deficits.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Vance
